svg.text: Height forms: what the ground can do on a hole
Side profiles, tee on the left, heights drawn about four times too tall. Each is at its plainest: fit it to the land and pair it with a fairway form.
Not drawn: saddle (through a notch between two knolls), reverse camber (a dogleg leaning out of its bend), kick plate (a bank that feeds a green).
A face under a level top. Short of it: a blind second
from below. On top: a flat lie and the view. The longest
Cut along a slope, sideways and up, 8–12%. Everything
feeds low; the high side has the angle; the ball is
Tee and landing area both high, a deep dip between. The
drive that does not carry rolls back to the bottom.
Two or three levels. The upper one sees the green; the
lower is easier to reach and leaves it blind.
Carry the crest and the far slope adds 30–40 yd. Land
short and the ball stops on the upslope.
A crowned fairway that sheds a ball to either side.
A valley fairway whose banks feed a loose drive back to
the middle. A helper: good for an opener.
A green up on a knob behind a steep front. Short rolls
back 20 yd; the shot must carry all the way.
A deep swale just short of the green. Carry it, or run
the ball down and up through it.
The ground runs away from you into the green. Land
short and let it release; fly it to the flag and it is
Up to a shelf where only the flag shows. Club up; short
Level, tee to green, with nothing between. The eye says
